Solutions 1–3 all give wrong areas. Working the problem independently gives **200**.

Place the external homothety centre at the origin with the bisector on the x-axis, and let the tangent lines make half-angle α with it. Let the centres be at distances D₁, D₂ from the origin. Then r_i = D_i sin α, and the contact chords of the two circles are vertical segments of lengths 2r_i cos α at x = D_i cos²α. The quadrilateral is a trapezoid with area (r₁+r₂)|D₂−D₁|cos³α = sin α cos³α (D₁+D₂)|D₂−D₁|.

The radical axis is x = c, and the common chord gives P = (c, 5). The distances from P to the two tangents are |c sin α ∓ 5 cos α|, which must be 3 and 12. This forces cos α = 9/10, sin α = √19/10, and c sin α = 7.5.

The power-of-a-point conditions give 0.81D² − 2cD + (c² + 25) = 0 for each D_i, with c = 75/√19. From this:
- D₁ + D₂ = 2c/0.81 = 5000/(27√19)
- (D₂ − D₁)² = 144/0.6561, so |D₂ − D₁| = 400/27

The area is therefore (√19/10)(729/1000)·(5000/(27√19))·(400/27) = 200. A numerical check (D₁ ≈ 28.68, D₂ ≈ 13.82, area ≈ 200.0) agrees.

CHOICE: NONE
CONFIDENCE: 4
